newsitem.title: USA: Clarcor sees Hastings unit profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Clarcor sees Hastings unit profit in 1997.

text.p: Clarcor Inc said problems at Hastings Filters are behind it and the unit is expected to show a profit in 1997 and reach an operating margin of eight to 10 percent by 1999.
Clarcor, a maker of filtration products, Monday reported net sales grew 14.9 percent to $333.3 million and net earnings grew 13.8 percent to $24.9 million in 1996 versus 1995.

"Fiscal 1996 included a full year of sales from Hastings Filters whereas fiscal 1995 included only one quarter of sales. Excluding Hastings Filters, net sales increased by 5.5 percent in fiscal 1996," the company said.
"We believe the problems we encountered at Hastings Filters in 1996, though not entirely unexpected, are now largely behind us," the company said.

Hastings had an operating loss of $2.2 million on the year, greater than projected. "This was due to added costs for outside component manufacturing and a rust problem on components purchased from the outside vendor," Clarcor said.

In addition, Clarcor said it completed an expansion of its Yankton, S.D., plant. "We can now produce virtually all of our filter components in-house and so better control manufacturing costs, inventory levels and quality," it said.
"Despite the loss, we have not changed any of our plans for Hastings nor have we reduced the capital we intend to invest in the business," it said.
Substantial cost savings and productivity improvements in 1997 are expected. "Our goal is to be one of the lowest cost (U.S.) producers of automotive filters," it said.

Excluding the Hastings loss and interest expense on the Hastings acquisition debt, Clarcor's operating margins would have been more than two percentage points higher and earnings per share would have been $0.12 to $0.13 per share higher than actually reported, the company said.

Elsewhere in its filtration products segment, Clarcor said Baldwin Filters sales rose more than 6.5 percent in 1996 and operating profits rose more than 12 percent. "We expect further progress at Baldwin in 1997," the company said.

In its consumer products segment, the Clark Filter unit's operating profit increased more than 20 percent on an 8.6 percent sales gain, the company said. The Airguard Industries unit improved operating margins by over three percentage points on an increase in sales of 3.8 percent, Clarcor said.
Finally, the company said, "Our international operations and export sales have grown to nearly 15 percent of total consolidated sales and we expect further progress."
